item.title: Drill 2026-10-01: reverse a clamp function (cmov)
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (MSVC convention: args in `ecx`, `edx`, `r8d`; return in `eax`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: mov eax, ecx cmp eax, edx cmovl eax, edx cmp eax, r8d cmovg eax, r8d ret ```
What does `mystery(int x, int lo, int hi)` return?
---
## Answer
```c int mystery(int x, int lo, int hi) { if (x < lo) x = lo; if (x > hi) x = hi; return x; } ```
It clamps `x` into the range `[lo, hi]` (if `lo > hi`, it returns `hi`).
## Explanation
- `cmovl`/`cmovg` copy the source into `eax` only if the signed condition from the preceding `cmp` holds — a branchless `if`, with no jumps. - First pair: `cmp eax, edx` then `cmovl` raises `x` to `lo` when `x < lo`. - Second pair: `cmp eax, r8d` then `cmovg` lowers the result to `hi` when it exceeds `hi`; `l`/`g` mean signed compares.
